options.text: Contain Gold 2 as carrier and keep net-side lane closed

questions.explanation: The reception changes who can attack net, so switch scan and contain; if Gold 2 is covered, return to next threat.

questions.prompt: Why does the failed pinch change your first skating lane?
questions.explanation: Possession moved to Gold and inside support is closer to net, so middle recovery protects the highest-risk route; if Navy recovers, transition roles change.

reasons.issue: The scene briefing contains the recurring bank-wide 'YOU is' subject-verb agreement defect: 'YOU is nearest recovering forward' instead of 'YOU are nearest recovering forward'. This is the same defect class documented across 27 prior packets as a real, consistent authoring mistake (never house style), and it sits in shared scene text, so it degrades the grammar check for every linked question even though five of the six questions' own text did not change.
reasons.change: Changed only the briefing clause from 'YOU is nearest recovering forward; Gold 2 cuts inside.' to 'YOU are nearest recovering forward; Gold 2 cuts inside.' No actor, coordinate, cue, source, or question-4/5/6 text was touched. Version incremented from 2 to 3.
reasons.evidence: Direct read of the version-2 briefing text in packets/packet-28.json: the phrase 'YOU is nearest recovering forward' is present verbatim. A prior repair recorded in docs/factory/research/question-review/repairs/u13-repairs.json (baseVersion 1 -> 2) fixed a different sentence in this same briefing (replacing raw +x/-x coordinate wording with 'Navy attacks Gold's net and defends Navy's net'), but that repair did not touch this 'YOU is' phrase, which survived unfixed into version 2.

reasons.issue: The same prior repair (docs/factory/research/question-review/repairs/u13-repairs.json, finding id 'u13-p2-dummy-distractors') replaced this question's original joke distractor ('The empty bench') with 'Whether an empty wall lane means Gold 1 cannot pass', but left the explanation text unchanged at 'bench is irrelevant' -- a stale reference to a distractor that no longer exists, which now actively confuses a learner reading the feedback. The replacement distractor text is also not grammatically parallel to options a/b (a 'whether...' clause versus two possessive noun phrases), which the authoring contract requires ('Keep choices grammatically parallel and plausible').
reasons.change: Reworded option c from 'Whether an empty wall lane means Gold 1 cannot pass' to 'An assumed empty passing lane for Gold 1' (a parallel noun phrase carrying the same false-inference teaching point) and updated the explanation from '...so recover middle and communicate; bench is irrelevant.' to '...so recover middle and communicate; an empty-looking wall lane does not prove Gold 1 has no pass.' so the feedback actually names and explains the current distractor. Answer set (a,b) and both correct options' text are unchanged.
reasons.evidence: Direct comparison of the current packets/packet-28.json question text (option c = 'Whether an empty wall lane means Gold 1 cannot pass', explanation still says 'bench is irrelevant') against docs/factory/research/question-review/repairs/u13-repairs.json's recorded before/after for exp26b-u13-015-q2, which shows the bench-to-inference option swap but no corresponding explanation edit.

sourceChecks.scope: Fetched and read (Team Canada Program of Excellence U17 Technical Curriculum, (c) Hockey Canada 2008). PDF page 8 contains a 'Support - Defensive' section reading: 'The player defending against the puck carrier requires the support of teammates to ensure that they are active away from the puck carrier and position themselves in a manner that will eliminate the options of the puck carrier. Players must be able to read the offensive options available to the puck carrier and move to a position that minimizes or takes away these options.' This directly and genuinely supports the teaching point in both scenarios (a teammate away from the direct puck battle reading and covering the next-most-dangerous option). This is a U17/POE (national-team-track) source being adapted down to U13 house-league content, which is disclosed in the scenario's own 'use' field ('Supports the stated coaching principle... not source-certified') rather than presented as a U13-specific or rule-level citation.
